answer: Each agent must lock a refundable stake in a time-locked vault before it can trade: spinning up a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand deposits, and misbehavior forfeits the stake. A bridge service cross-checks each stake against activity on other ledgers, so one identity cannot reuse its reputation across markets, while a raven audit randomly challenges agents to prove control of their vault keys. Attack costs scale with every sockpuppet, while honest agents pay only a temporary deposit.
